_comment: The slot-sheet primitives, in one place, because adding one has to be taught to
FIVE consumers and every hand-maintained mirror of them has rotted at least once.
Consumers, all of which read this file:
1. lib/llm/slotSheet.ts       parsing and scoring
2. blocks/action/LLMAction.ts wiring the attribute into a call
3. lib/llm/probe.test.ts      reporting what a sheet enforces, for the audit
4. molly_scoring/olx_prompts  generating the prompt body from the rubric
5. molly_scoring/agreement.py the measurement harness's schema and scoring
Consumer 5 was added after it drifted three separate ways at once while its
docstring called itself a mirror of buildSlotSchema(): it left every computed
key in the response schema (27 keys, 14 items) so the model was required to
answer what the prompt told it not to; it never stripped the `@pts` suffix, so
35 slots offered `"no@2"` as a legal verdict; and it never expanded `counts`.
A registry protects the files that read it, and that one did not read it.
`excludes` says WHICH keys leave the schema: `key` for a check computed in
place, `members` for a rule whose keys are the things it stands in for. It
lives here because enforcement.py and agreement.py both need it and both had
their own copy of `if attr == "counts"`.
`equivalence.py --enforcement` checks conformance empirically rather than
trusting this list: for every primitive with excludesKeys, it asserts the
generated prompt omits those keys from the checklist, that it carries a line
telling the model not to answer them, AND that the schema the harness actually
sends omits them too. A registry that is only a declaration would rot the way
every other hand-maintained mirror in this project has.

primitives.summary: Checks that between them must COVER a set of labels; the grader does the pairing.
A check COMPUTED by comparing two others, with lenient operands that establish nothing.
A check charged only when another is satisfied; one deduction, two possible causes.
A check read off the page — field contents — rather than asked of the model.
A repeated element counted ONCE, with its member checks derived from the count.
